dialogues.speaker: Tiepolo
dialogues.text: Welcome, young one from afar. I welcome you in the name of the Consilium Sapientium. I am Petrichor's "Doge."

dialogues.speaker: Tiepolo
dialogues.text: If you trust the wisdom of an elder, then you may ask me anything.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Consilium Sapientium?

dialogues.speaker: Tiepolo
dialogues.text: Trust in the wisdom of the elderly is a tradition here. Since ancient times, all affairs in the town have been assessed by a committee of its elders.

dialogues.speaker: Tiepolo
dialogues.text: And of these elders, the most trustworthy would be selected as "Doge."

dialogues.speaker: Tiepolo
dialogues.text: And that is me, old and unskilled though I may be.

dialogues.speaker: Tiepolo
dialogues.text: Though given the role of overseer, I must say that there is little for me to oversee here. We live simple lives and have simple customs. All we do, we do by tradition.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't have any questions. Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Tiepolo
dialogues.text: Alright. I do hope you shall enjoy your stay here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Petrichor's customs...

dialogues.speaker: Tiepolo
dialogues.text: Petrichor is a romantic, idyllic place. People respect custom and are customarily polite and friendly to outside guests.

dialogues.speaker: Tiepolo
dialogues.text: Of course, some of us go a little overboard, and as a result may seem almost... wary, perhaps.

dialogues.speaker: Tiepolo
dialogues.text: But do forgive us. Petrichor is far from the Court of Fontaine, and people here have hardly ever left the town.

dialogues.speaker: Tiepolo
dialogues.text: Just as a stone thrown into an ancient well can stir up ripples, people always fear that outlanders may disturb our peace.

dialogues.speaker: Tiepolo
dialogues.text: So please, do not hold it against them!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Petrichor's history...

dialogues.speaker: Tiepolo
dialogues.text: Haha! Well, there's much to tell. Petrichor's got a history longer than the Court of Fontaine, after all — so long that ten operas wouldn't be enough to get through it all.

dialogues.speaker: Tiepolo
dialogues.text: Five hundred years ago, this place was still governed by the de Petrichor family, and their lineage had long ruled here.

dialogues.speaker: Tiepolo
dialogues.text: That had been the case ever since the first Duke appointed by Egeria, and they were, one and all, just and benevolent leaders who guided the town to ever-increasing prosperity.

dialogues.speaker: Tiepolo
dialogues.text: Alas, the final patrono of the family was transferred to be mayor of Poisson — there, he lost his life, and there did the family tree wither.

dialogues.speaker: Tiepolo
dialogues.text: For a time after, it seemed as though the town would become some abandoned fishing village... At least until after our first Doge Ruggiero established the Consilium Sapientium and restored our fortunes.

dialogues.speaker: Tiepolo
dialogues.text: The townspeople at that time believed that the town fell into ruin because of our relations with the outside world grew too close, destroying our traditions.

dialogues.speaker: Tiepolo
dialogues.text: That said, our youngsters believe differently nowadays. That fellow Foscari's been advocating that it's time for change, too.
